entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Richard Foxe was an English churchman and founder of Corpus Christi College, Oxford.

Born around 1470, Foxe rose through the ranks of the Church of England to become Bishop of Exeter, Bath and Wells, Durham, and Winchester. He also served as Lord Privy Seal under King Henry VIII.

Foxe's legacy extends to his role in shaping the Church of England, particularly during the reign of his powerful patron, Henry VIII. The college he founded in Oxford remains a prestigious institution to this day.

Richard Foxe's life was marked by his unwavering dedication to the Church of England, which would go on to shape the course of English history. His influence can still be felt in the modern Church of England, and his legacy serves as a testament to the enduring power of faith and leadership.

In the end, Foxe's story is one of faith, perseverance, and the unyielding pursuit of a vision. His impact on the Church of England and the world beyond will be remembered for generations to come.
